data.raw_text:
BREAKING 
CHINA: RADAR LOCKED
PHILIPPINES: TARGET SIGHTED AND LOCKED AS WELL 📷
MARITIME STANDOFF | PHILIPPINE NAVY STANDS ITS GROUND
In the contested waters of the West Philippine Sea, the BRP Miguel Malvar (FFG-06) did not flinch.
While conducting a lawful sovereignty patrol near Sabina Shoal on March 07, 2026, the Philippine warship was confronted by a PLA Navy corvette hull 622 that escalated tensions by directing its fire-control radar a hostile act that, in naval warfare, is indistinguishable from preparing to engage.
But this time, the Philippines was not a passive observer.
The BRP Miguel Malvar immediately detected the radar lock through its advanced sensor suite. Within seconds, alarms were triggered, combat systems were activated, and the crew moved to battle stations with precision and discipline. A firm radio challenge was issued but more importantly, the frigate responded with action.
Using its electro-optical targeting systems, the Philippine warship locked onto the Chinese vessel placing it under direct tracking and silent warning: any further escalation would be met in kind.
For a brief but critical moment, both ships stood on the edge of confrontation one probing, the other fully prepared to respond.
The outcome was decisive.
The PLA Navy vessel disengaged its radar and backed down. as well.
Photos from Philippine Navy
